scenes.dialogue: I have twenty things to do and I'm so overwhelmed I can't even begin.
scenes.caption: Looking at everything all at once overwhelms the brain and creates paralysis.

scenes.dialogue: If I can't finish all twenty things today, what's the point of starting?
scenes.caption: All-or-nothing thinking magnifies tasks into an insurmountable wall.

scenes.dialogue: Wait. I don't have to conquer the whole mountain in this single hour.
scenes.caption: Pausing interrupts the freeze: separate the total pile from the next five minutes.

scenes.dialogue: You do not have to conquer all twenty tasks simultaneously.
scenes.caption: Break the wall down into a single brick. Momentum follows action, not perfection.

scenes.dialogue: Pick the simplest sub-task on your list—something that takes under 5 minutes.
scenes.caption: One small step forward breaks the freeze and builds genuine momentum.

scenes.dialogue: Everyone is doing so much better than me... I'm completely behind.
scenes.caption: Curated achievements of others easily trigger deep personal inadequacy.

scenes.dialogue: I keep looping through how far ahead everyone else is compared to me.
scenes.caption: Comparing your internal struggle to external highlights feeds the spiral.

scenes.dialogue: Wait. Their public highlights don't define my personal journey.
scenes.caption: Separate other people's curated milestones from your own authentic values.

scenes.dialogue: Other people's pace is not my measuring tape. My journey has its own timing.
scenes.caption: Replace upward social comparison with alignment to your own intrinsic values and pace.

scenes.dialogue: I will set my phone aside and focus on what genuinely matters to my own growth.
scenes.caption: Direct your attention inward toward your own growth, craft, and authentic progress.

scenes.dialogue: I don't know what will happen with my future, and the uncertainty feels terrifying.
scenes.caption: When the future feels ambiguous, the mind anticipates threat where there is only unknown.

scenes.dialogue: What if something terrible happens and I'm powerless to handle it?
scenes.caption: Demanding certainty from an unpredictable future fuels escalating dread.

scenes.dialogue: Wait. Not knowing what happens next doesn't mean catastrophe is guaranteed.
scenes.caption: Pausing separates the feeling of uncertainty from the certainty of threat.

scenes.dialogue: I cannot predict the entire future today. I can handle the hour in front of me.
scenes.caption: Reframing shifts focus from demanding future certainty to exercising present agency.

scenes.dialogue: I will anchor in today's routine tasks and take it one steady hour at a time.
scenes.caption: Grounding in immediate present action relieves the burden of carrying tomorrow's unknowns.
